turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.text:
I'll investigate this using the gh CLI without cloning.Good set of core files. Let me examine the core streaming implementation and then trace which API methods use it.Now let's check `responses.ts` for the Responses API streaming, and `_client.post` in the core client to confirm how `stream: true` flows to `defaultParseResponse`.Now let's check the other resources with streaming: audio/transcriptions.ts, images.ts, beta/threads (Assistants API runs), and beta/realtime.This confirms the wiring: `client.post()` → `makeRequest` → `APIPromise` (default parser is `defaultParseResponse` in `src/internal/parse.ts`) → checks `options.stream` → `Stream.fromSSEResponse` in `src/core/streaming.ts`. I have enough to answer comprehensively.Confirmed. Here's the full picture.

## Core streaming implementation

**`src/core/streaming.ts`** — the actual SSE/stream parsing engine. Key symbols:
- `class Stream<Item> implements AsyncIterable<Item>` — wraps a `fetch` `Response` or `ReadableStream` into an async-iterable stream of typed items.
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse(response, controller, client, synthesizeEventData)` — parses a raw `Response` as Server-Sent Events, splitting on `data: [DONE]`, JSON-parsing each `data:` line, and surfacing API errors embedded in the stream.
- `Stream.fromReadableStream(readableStream, controller, client)` — parses a newline-delimited JSON `ReadableStream` (used to rehydrate a stream that was piped through `toReadableStream()`, e.g. proxied to a browser client).
- `_iterSSEMessages()` / `iterSSEChunks()` / `class SSEDecoder` — low-level SSE framing (byte buffering on double-newline boundaries, `event:`/`data:` field parsing).

`src/streaming.ts` is just a deprecated re-export (`export * from './core/streaming'`) kept for backwards compatibility.

**`src/internal/parse.ts`** is the dispatch point: `defaultParseResponse()` checks `props.options.stream` — if true, it calls `props.options.__streamClass?.fromSSEResponse(...)` (a per-endpoint override) or falls back to `Stream.fromSSEResponse(...)`. This function is the `parseResponse` callback used by every `APIPromise` (`src/core/api-promise.ts`), which itself is returned from `this._client.post(...)` calls in resource methods (`src/client.ts:749`, `makeRequest`).

## Public API methods that route into it

Every one of these overloads `stream: true/false` in params and passes `stream: body.stream ?? false` to `this._client.post(...)`, returning `APIPromise<Stream<T>>`:

| Method | File | Event type |
|---|---|---|
| `client.chat.completions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:61-79` | `Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>` |
| `client.completions.create({stream:true})` (legacy) | `src/resources/completions.ts:28-43` | `Stream<Completion>` |
| `client.responses.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:96-122` | `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` |
| `client.responses.retrieve({stream:true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:137-168` | `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` |
| `client.images.generate({stream:true})` | `src/resources/images.ts:75-93` | `Stream<ImageGenStreamEvent>` |
| `client.images.edit({stream:true})` | `src/resources/images.ts:45-61` | `Stream<ImageEditStreamEvent>` |
| `client.audio.transcriptions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/audio/transcriptions.ts:31-62` | `Stream<TranscriptionStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.createAndRun({stream:true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/threads.ts:143-163` | `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:57-82` | `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.submitToolOutputs({stream:true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:246-272` | `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` |

**Higher-level convenience wrappers** (build on `Stream`, add event-emitter/accumulation ergonomics, in `src/lib/`):
- `client.chat.completions.stream(body)` → `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion` (`src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts`), extends `src/lib/AbstractChatCompletionRunner.ts`. Also `runTools()` with `stream: true` routes to `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner` (`src/lib/ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts`).
- `client.responses.stream(body)` → `ResponseStream.createResponse` (`src/lib/responses/ResponseStream.ts`).
- `client.beta.threads.createAndRunStream(body)` and `client.beta.threads.runs.stream(...)` / `.createAndStream(...)` (deprecated) / `.submitToolOutputsStream(...)` → all funnel into `AssistantStream` (`src/lib/AssistantStream.ts`), which extends the base `src/lib/EventStream.ts` (`class EventStream<EventTypes>`).

All of these `lib/*Stream.ts` classes ultimately call `Stream.fromSSEResponse` or `Stream.fromReadableStream` from `src/core/streaming.ts` internally (e.g. `ChatCompletionStream._fromReadableStream` at `src/lib/ChatCompletionStream.ts:394` calls `Stream.fromReadableStream`).

**Separate mechanism, not SSE:** `client.beta.realtime` (`src/resources/beta/realtime/realtime.ts`) uses WebSockets, not `core/streaming.ts` at all — it's a distinct transport for the Realtime API.

## What I did not verify
- I didn't inspect `src/lib/AbstractChatCompletionRunner.ts` or `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts` line-by-line (only confirmed they exist and are imported/used for `runTools`).
- I didn't verify the WebSocket implementation details of `beta.realtime` (only confirmed by grep that it doesn't reference `Stream`/SSE).
- I relied on GitHub's code search index and the `main` branch tree as of now (2026-07-04); did not check version/tag history for how this evolved.
- I did not execute/test any code — this is static analysis of file contents only (per your instruction not to clone).
